alignments.note: Anarthrous dative participle rendered as a finite relative clause with a supplied antecedent pronoun. No Greek article stands here, so rules 31/32 do not divide anything: the supplied *To him* and the relativizer *that* are rule 7 helpers on the participle, *To* realizing the dative case under rule 21's reasoning. Rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical verb *knoweth* rather than on the pronoun or relativizer. The discontinuity across t003 is licensed by rule 15 and absorbs nothing.
Inferential conjunction on its own English word.
No conjunction and no preposition governs the infinitive, so the infinitival *to* is rule 7's ordinary helper on its verb (rules 40 and 61), and the unit heads on the lexical verb.

Anarthrous adjective as object of the infinitive; the ASV supplies no determiner, so the adjective stands alone on its own word. Split from the infinitive under rule 2 since both English realizations are independently recoverable.
Coordinating conjunction joining the two participles, realized by *and*. An expressed Greek conjunction, so rules 88 and 98 on a supplied juncture are not in question.

The participle takes the supplied object pronoun *it*, which resumes the preceding infinitive phrase. Rule 103 names a resumptive pronoun as its contrast case, rule 7 listing pronouns among the helpers that belong to the word licensing them; rule 74's supplied-object clause then fixes where it goes, keeping it on the verb that requires it in English. Two competing readings: `added` lexical resumption under rule 103, rejected because *it* is a pronoun and not full lexical content; or folding *it* onto s003/s004 on the shape of 3JN.1.13's *them* on `Πολλά`, rejected because there the antecedent was a single expressed word taking a discontinuous second realization, whereas here the antecedent is the whole phrase `καλὸν ποιεῖν` and any single carrier would be arbitrary.

Ordinary negative with the participle, aligned to *not*. Rules 41 and 59 do not apply: no negative indefinite stands in the clause for the negation to be spelt into. The crossed order against t010/t011 is English word order only.

Resumptive dative pronoun; the case preposition *to* rides with it under rule 21's reasoning, headed on the pronoun. Distinct from the participle's own supplied *To him* at t001/t002, which the ASV writes separately.

The expressed copula takes the supplied dummy subject *it* as a rule 7/9 helper, headed on the verb rather than the subject. Rules 53, 63 and 96 are not in question, the Greek verb being expressed rather than supplied.
Anarthrous predicate noun on its own word. The copula is expressed in Greek, so nothing supplied needs carrying here and the noun stands alone.

review_notes: Kept the accepted alignment unchanged in structure and heads; the only edit is an expanded note on s007 recording the two competing readings and why each was rejected, per rule 16.

All 10 source ids and all 17 target ids are partitioned exactly once. Every unit is `aligned`; there are no unrepresented, added or noncompositional units, and no verse in this projection is orphaned across a versification seam (rules 37, 97 not in play).

s007 is the one materially contestable unit. *it* has three defensible homes: on the participle as a supplied object (taken), `added` under rule 103, or folded onto the antecedent s003/s004 on the shape of 3JN.1.13. Rule 74 states in terms that a supplied object stays with the verb that requires it in English, and rule 103 names a resumptive pronoun as its own contrast case, so the taken reading rests on two explicit contract statements rather than on analogy.

s001 has no Greek article, so rule 32's split of a substantival article from its participle is not triggered and rule 90 does not bear on it; the supplied antecedent pronoun and the relativizer both stay with the participle as rule 7 helpers, headed on *knoweth* under rule 17.

The two English *to him* phrases are not a double realization of one token: t001/t002 is the participle's supplied antecedent with the dative case preposition riding along, and t013/t014 is the resumptive `αὐτῷ`. Rule 103's repeated-lexical-content test does not reach them, both being pronouns the ASV writes for distinct source tokens.

s010 keeps the supplied dummy *it* because the Greek copula is expressed; the supplied-copula chain of rules 53/62/63/68/96 governs only verbless clauses and has no application here, so `ἁμαρτία` correctly stands bare on t017.
